claims.statement: The paper calls Tom Allen the champion pugilist of America.

claims.statement: Tom Allen returned home to St. Louis from Cincinnati, where he had spent a few days with his old English sweetheart.
claims.excerpt: returned bome yesterday from Cincinna‘l, where he spent a few days with his old Epglish sweetheart,

claims.statement: Tom Allen arrived in Louisville about 5 o'clock on July 5, 1869, by train from Cincinnati.
claims.excerpt: He arrivedin Louisville about 5 o’clock, in time

claims.statement: Tom Allen gave a sparring exhibition at Benson's Theatre in Louisville on July 5, 1869, where the hall was crowded.
claims.excerpt: befcre the sparring commenced the ball was crowded

claims.statement: Tom Allen had a set-to with his trainer and travelling companion Jim Coyne at the Louisville exhibition.
claims.excerpt: to with Jim Coyne, bis trainer and travelling com-

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he was willing to fight any man in America for a purse of $1,000 to $5,000.
claims.excerpt: willing to fight anv manu in America for a puree of $1000 to $5000

claims.statement: Tom Allen offered to put up $2,500 against Charley Gallagher's $1,500 for a rematch.
claims.excerpt: he 1s willing to put up $2500 agains; Charley’s $1500.

claims.statement: Tom Allen wants his fight with Charley Gallagher to take place within fifty miles of Cincinnati.
claims.excerpt: Tom wants to fight within fifty miles of Cincinnati.

claims.statement: Charley Gallagher knocked out Tom Allen with a lucky blow in the second round, the winter before July 1869.
claims.excerpt: who laid him out last winter by a lucky blow in the second round

claims.statement: Tom Allen won the late prize fight against Mike McCoole.

notes: Dates: the paper is dated 8 July, so 'yesterday' is 7 July for the return home. The Louisville arrival is 5 July, from the Courier of the 6th. The article's fight with McCoole is only mentioned in passing.
